title: __init__ method is a generator.
summary: Used when the special class method __init__ is turned into a generator by a yield in its body. pylint calls it init-is-generator.

title: Explicit return in __init__.
summary: Used when the special class method __init__ has an explicit return value. pylint calls it return-in-init.

title: … already defined line ….
summary: Used when a function / class / method is redefined. pylint calls it function-redefined.

title: … not properly in loop.
summary: Used when break or continue keywords are used outside a loop. pylint calls it not-in-loop.

title: Return outside function.
summary: Used when a "return" statement is found outside a function or method. pylint calls it return-outside-function.

title: Yield outside function.
summary: Used when a "yield" statement is found outside a function or method. pylint calls it yield-outside-function.

title: Return with argument inside generator.
summary: Used when a "return" statement with an argument is found in a generator function or method (e.g. with some "yield" statements). This message can't be emitted when using Python >= 3.3. pylint calls it return-arg-in-generator.

title: Use of the non-existent … operator.
summary: Used when you attempt to use the C-style pre-increment or pre-decrement operator -- and ++, which doesn't exist in Python. pylint calls it nonexistent-operator.

title: Duplicate argument name … in function definition.
summary: Duplicate argument names in function definitions are syntax errors. pylint calls it duplicate-argument-name.
message_templates: Duplicate argument name {} in function definition

title: Abstract class … with abstract methods instantiated.
summary: Used when an abstract class with abc.ABCMeta as metaclass has abstract methods and is instantiated. pylint calls it abstract-class-instantiated.
message_templates: Abstract class {} with abstract methods instantiated

title: The first reversed() argument is not a sequence.
summary: Used when the first argument to reversed() builtin isn't a sequence (does not implement __reversed__, nor __getitem__ and __len__. pylint calls it bad-reversed-sequence.
message_templates: The first reversed() argument is not a sequence

title: More than one starred expression in assignment.
summary: Emitted when there are more than one starred expressions (*x) in an assignment. This is a SyntaxError. pylint calls it too-many-star-expressions.
message_templates: More than one starred expression in assignment

title: Starred assignment target must be in a list or tuple.
summary: Emitted when a star expression is used as a starred assignment target. pylint calls it invalid-star-assignment-target.
message_templates: Starred assignment target must be in a list or tuple

title: Can use starred expression only in assignment target.
summary: Emitted when a star expression is not used in an assignment target. pylint calls it star-needs-assignment-target.
message_templates: Can use starred expression only in assignment target

title: Name … is nonlocal and global.
summary: Emitted when a name is both nonlocal and global. pylint calls it nonlocal-and-global.

title: Nonlocal name … found without binding.
summary: Emitted when a nonlocal variable does not have an attached name somewhere in the parent scopes. pylint calls it nonlocal-without-binding.

title: Name … is used prior to global declaration.
summary: Emitted when a name is used prior a global declaration, which results in an error since Python 3.6. This message can't be emitted when using Python < 3.6. pylint calls it used-prior-global-declaration.
message_templates: Name {} is used prior to global declaration

title: Format function is not called on str.
summary: Emitted when format function is not called on str object. e.g doing print("value: {}").format(123) instead of print("value: {}".format(123)). This might not be what the user intended to do. pylint calls it misplaced-format-function.
message_templates: format function is not called on str

title: An attribute defined in … line … hides this method.
summary: Used when a class defines a method which is hidden by an instance attribute from an ancestor class or set by some client code. pylint calls it method-hidden.
message_templates: An attribute defined in {} line {} hides this method

title: Access to member … before its definition line ….
summary: Used when an instance member is accessed before it's actually assigned. pylint calls it access-member-before-definition.
message_templates: Access to member {} before its definition line {}

title: Method … has no argument.
summary: Used when a method which should have the bound instance as first argument has no argument defined. pylint calls it no-method-argument.

title: Method … should have "self" as first argument.
summary: Used when a method has an attribute different the "self" as first argument. This is considered as an error since this is a so common convention that you shouldn't break it!. pylint calls it no-self-argument.
message_templates: Method {} should have "self" as first argument

title: Invalid object … in __slots__, must contain only non empty strings.
summary: Used when an invalid (non-string) object occurs in __slots__. pylint calls it invalid-slots-object.
message_templates: Invalid object {} in __slots__, must contain only non empty strings

title: Assigning to attribute … not defined in class slots.
summary: Used when assigning to an attribute not defined in the class slots. pylint calls it assigning-non-slot.
message_templates: Assigning to attribute {} not defined in class slots

title: Invalid __slots__ object.
summary: Used when an invalid __slots__ is found in class. Only a string, an iterable or a sequence is permitted. pylint calls it invalid-slots.

title: Inheriting …, which is not a class.
summary: Used when a class inherits from something which is not a class. pylint calls it inherit-non-class.
message_templates: Inheriting {}, which is not a class.

title: Inconsistent method resolution order for class ….
summary: Used when a class has an inconsistent method resolution order. pylint calls it inconsistent-mro.
message_templates: Inconsistent method resolution order for class {}

title: Duplicate bases for class ….
summary: Duplicate use of base classes in derived classes raise TypeErrors. pylint calls it duplicate-bases.

title: Value … in slots conflicts with class variable.
summary: Used when a value in __slots__ conflicts with a class variable, property or method. pylint calls it class-variable-slots-conflict.
message_templates: Value {} in slots conflicts with class variable

title: Invalid assignment to '__class__'. Should be a class definition but got a '…'.
summary: Used when an invalid object is assigned to a __class__ property. Only a class is permitted. pylint calls it invalid-class-object.
message_templates: Invalid assignment to '__class__'. Should be a class definition but got a '{}'

title: Extending inherited Enum class "…".
summary: Used when a class tries to extend an inherited Enum class. Doing so will raise a TypeError at runtime. pylint calls it invalid-enum-extension.

title: No such name … in __slots__.
summary: Raised when a type annotation on a class is absent from the list of names in __slots__, and __slots__ does not contain a __dict__ entry. pylint calls it declare-non-slot.

title: __iter__ returns non-iterator.
summary: Used when an __iter__ method returns something which is not an iterable (i.e. has no __next__ method). pylint calls it non-iterator-returned.

title: The special method … expects … param(s), … … given.
summary: Emitted when a special method was defined with an invalid number of parameters. If it has too few or too many, it might not work at all. pylint calls it unexpected-special-method-signature.
message_templates: The special method {} expects {} param(s), {} {} given

title: __len__ does not return non-negative integer.
summary: Used when a __len__ method returns something which is not a non-negative integer. pylint calls it invalid-length-returned.

title: __bool__ does not return bool.
summary: Used when a __bool__ method returns something which is not a bool. pylint calls it invalid-bool-returned.

title: __index__ does not return int.
summary: Used when an __index__ method returns something which is not an integer. pylint calls it invalid-index-returned.

title: __repr__ does not return str.
summary: Used when a __repr__ method returns something which is not a string. pylint calls it invalid-repr-returned.

title: __str__ does not return str.
summary: Used when a __str__ method returns something which is not a string. pylint calls it invalid-str-returned.

title: __bytes__ does not return bytes.
summary: Used when a __bytes__ method returns something which is not bytes. pylint calls it invalid-bytes-returned.

title: __hash__ does not return int.
summary: Used when a __hash__ method returns something which is not an integer. pylint calls it invalid-hash-returned.

title: __length_hint__ does not return non-negative integer.
summary: Used when a __length_hint__ method returns something which is not a non-negative integer. pylint calls it invalid-length-hint-returned.

title: __format__ does not return str.
summary: Used when a __format__ method returns something which is not a string. pylint calls it invalid-format-returned.

title: __getnewargs__ does not return a tuple.
summary: Used when a __getnewargs__ method returns something which is not a tuple. pylint calls it invalid-getnewargs-returned.

title: __getnewargs_ex__ does not return a tuple containing (tuple, dict).
summary: Used when a __getnewargs_ex__ method returns something which is not of the form tuple(tuple, dict). pylint calls it invalid-getnewargs-ex-returned.
message_templates: __getnewargs_ex__ does not return a tuple containing (tuple, dict)

title: Unable to import ….
summary: Used when pylint has been unable to import a module. pylint calls it import-error.

title: Attempted relative import beyond top-level package.
summary: Used when a relative import tries to access too many levels in the current package. pylint calls it relative-beyond-top-level.
message_templates: Attempted relative import beyond top-level package

title: Lazy import is not allowed ….
summary: Emitted when a PEP 810 lazy import is used where Python forbids it: inside a function, a class body or a try statement, or as a wildcard import. This is a SyntaxError. This message can't be emitted when using Python < 3.15. pylint calls it invalid-lazy-import.

title: Using variable … before assignment.
summary: Emitted when a local variable is accessed before its assignment took place. Assignments in try blocks are assumed not to have occurred when evaluating associated except/finally blocks. Assignments in except blocks are assumed not to have occurred when evaluating statements outside the block, except when the associated try block contains a return statement. pylint calls it used-before-assignment.

title: Undefined variable ….
summary: Used when an undefined variable is accessed. pylint calls it undefined-variable.

title: Undefined variable name … in __all__.
summary: Used when an undefined variable name is referenced in __all__. pylint calls it undefined-all-variable.

title: Invalid object … in __all__, must contain only strings.
summary: Used when an invalid (non-string) object occurs in __all__. pylint calls it invalid-all-object.
message_templates: Invalid object {} in __all__, must contain only strings

title: Invalid format for __all__, must be tuple or list.
summary: Used when __all__ has an invalid format. pylint calls it invalid-all-format.
message_templates: Invalid format for __all__, must be tuple or list

title: Possibly using variable … before assignment.
summary: Emitted when a local variable is accessed before its assignment took place in both branches of an if/else switch. pylint calls it possibly-used-before-assignment.

title: No name … in module ….
summary: Used when a name cannot be found in a module. pylint calls it no-name-in-module.

title: Attempting to unpack a non-sequence….
summary: Used when something which is not a sequence is used in an unpack assignment. pylint calls it unpacking-non-sequence.

title: Invalid index for iterable length.
summary: Emitted when an index used on an iterable goes beyond the length of that iterable. pylint calls it potential-index-error.

title: Bad except clauses order (…).
summary: Used when except clauses are not in the correct order (from the more specific to the more generic). If you don't fix the order, some exceptions may not be caught by the most specific handler. pylint calls it bad-except-order.

title: Raising … while only classes or instances are allowed.
summary: Used when something which is neither a class nor an instance is raised (i.e. a TypeError will be raised). pylint calls it raising-bad-type.
message_templates: Raising {} while only classes or instances are allowed

title: The raise statement is not inside an except clause.
summary: Used when a bare raise is not used inside an except clause. This generates an error, since there are no active exceptions to be reraised. An exception to this rule is represented by a bare raise inside a finally clause, which might work, as long as an exception is raised inside the try block, but it is nevertheless a code smell that must not be relied upon. pylint calls it misplaced-bare-raise.
message_templates: The raise statement is not inside an except clause

title: Exception cause set to something which is not an exception, nor None.
summary: Used when using the syntax "raise ... from ...", where the exception cause is not an exception, nor None. pylint calls it bad-exception-cause.
message_templates: Exception cause set to something which is not an exception, nor None

title: Raising a class which doesn't inherit from BaseException.
summary: Used when a class which doesn't inherit from BaseException is raised. pylint calls it raising-non-exception.
message_templates: Raising a class which doesn't inherit from BaseException

title: NotImplemented raised - should raise NotImplementedError.
summary: Used when NotImplemented is raised instead of NotImplementedError. pylint calls it notimplemented-raised.

title: Catching an exception which doesn't inherit from Exception: ….
summary: Used when a class which doesn't inherit from Exception is used as an exception in an except clause. pylint calls it catching-non-exception.
message_templates: Catching an exception which doesn't inherit from Exception: {}
